route.text: State Baker–Harman–Pintz (primes in (x, x + x^(21/40)), at least c x^(21/40) / log x of them) as one have, and derive the node from it by mapping natural primes injectively into the node's integer set.

terminal_goal_state.text:
have h_bhp : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ x₀ : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, x₀ ≤ x →
    c * x ^ (21 / 40 : ℝ) / Real.log x ≤
      (((Finset.range ⌈x + x ^ (21 / 40 : ℝ)⌉₊).filter
        (fun p : ℕ => p.Prime ∧ x < (p : ℝ) ∧ (p : ℝ) < x + x ^ (21 / 40 : ℝ))).card : ℝ)

references.note: Final display, p. 562: 'for all large x, pi(x + x^0.525) - pi(x) > (x^0.525/log x)(1 - 0.3 - 0.06 - 0.21 - 0.34) = 9 x^0.525/(100 log x)'. Read in the PDF (cs.umd.edu copy) on 2026-10-14. Theorem 1 itself is stated for the backward interval [x - x^0.525, x]; the counting bound at the end is for the forward interval, which is this node's.
references.title: R. C. Baker, G. Harman and J. Pintz, The difference between consecutive primes, II, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 83 (2001) 532-562

literature_proposed.summary: This node is BHP 2001's counting bound in the forward form: with C = 9/100 (any C slightly below it, to absorb the strict upper endpoint k < p < k + k^0.525 and integer k, at most one prime of difference), for all k beyond some k0 there are at least C k^0.525 / log k primes in (k, k + k^0.525). Exponent 21/40 = 0.525 matches, log is natural log, the k0 is ineffective-as-stated (BHP say it could be made effective with effort). The match between the paper's display and this Lean statement is my reading, not checked by anyone else; nothing of BHP is formalised. Note BHP's sieve is not a routine formalisation, so 'known', not 'elementary'.

import Mathlib
import Nodes.«erdos-1094--h2--h2--h1».Context

open scoped Nat

/-! Hole `h_bhp` of a merged partial proof, as a node (D-12 #5, D-29).
Statement generated by the gate from the assembly; immutable (D-3). -/

theorem erdos_1094__h2__h2__h1 : ∃ (C : ℝ),
  (0 : ℝ) < C ∧
    ∃ (k₀ : ℕ),
      ∀ (k : ℕ),
        k₀ ≤ k →
          C * (↑k : ℝ) ^ (21 / 40 : ℝ) / Real.log (↑k : ℝ) ≤
            (↑{p ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊(↑k : ℝ)⌋ ⌈(↑k : ℝ) + (↑k : ℝ) ^ (21 / 40 : ℝ)⌉ |
                    (0 : ℤ) < p ∧
                      Nat.Prime p.natAbs ∧ (↑k : ℝ) < (↑p : ℝ) ∧ (↑p : ℝ) < (↑k : ℝ) + (↑k : ℝ) ^ (21 / 40 : ℝ)}.card :
              ℝ) := by
  sorry
